content:
After months of developer and public beta stages, Apple is now rolling out macOS 26.6 for all users with compatible Macs. Here's what the update includes.

macOS 26.6 is now available

macOS 26.6 has been released, fixing over 150 security vulnerabilities, along with other bug fixes and performance improvements. These include a fix for an issue that incorrectly displayed deprecation notices for some Intel-only apps, as well as bugs affecting HealthKit and HDR screenshots in Messages.

For users planning to upgrade to macOS 27 Golden Gate later this year, macOS 26.6 has likely begun indexing for the new Siri AI, the new Siri app, and other features related to the new Apple Intelligence.

Apple has so far only confirmed this process for iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, but the Mac side appears to be doing the same. Users on the macOS 27 beta will know that the indexing process takes several days, so starting now should help reduce the wait time when upgrading later.

The official version of macOS 26.6 is build 25G72, which differs from last week's release candidate version (25G70).

Have you found any new features in macOS 26.6? Let us know in the comments.
